misconfig_patterns: /metrics on port 8085 served without auth by default — velero_backup_* gauges leak every backup and schedule name plus counts/last-status/last-successful-timestamp
/debug/pprof/ on 6060 exposed when --profiler-address enabled — leaks goroutines/heap incl. in-flight bucket paths and credential env
World-readable BackupStorageLocation S3/Azure/GCS bucket reproduces Velero's own /backups/ folder listing for an anonymous reader

AI-scope discriminator: backups in scope only when velero-backup.json spec.includedNamespaces / resource-list.json.gz name AI/ML namespaces (kubeflow, mlflow, kserve, ray, seldon, triton) or backed-up CRD kinds (notebooks.kubeflow.org, inferenceservices.serving.kserve.io, rayclusters.ray.io) or vector-store PVC names (qdrant-, milvus-, weaviate-, chromadb-, pgvector); the kopia/<namespace>/ prefix names the namespace without reading a blob; generic substrate (plain Postgres/etcd, system namespaces) is OUT of scope

Restraint: names and manifests are the finding; reading /metrics labels and velero-backup.json/resource-list manifests is metadata; downloading contents.tar.gz, restic/kopia repo blobs, or PV snapshots is exfiltration of a whole-cluster image incl. secrets and is forbidden; POSTing a Velero Restore CR or any bucket write is a write/destructive primitive and forbidden

response_markers: # HELP velero_backup_total Current number of existent backups
podVolume_ prefix on node-agent /metrics (restic/kopia file-system backup)
active_probe.false_positive_check: Any Prometheus /metrics exposes go_*/process_* counters which do NOT confirm Velero. Require at least one velero_-prefixed series (velero_backup_total or a velero_backup_*{schedule=} label) and the literal velero_backup_total HELP line / native velero_ namespace, NOT a kube_customresource_* wrapper from kube-state-metrics, NOT http.title:Velero (matches seriohub/otwld dashboards + marketing pages with no velero_ series), NOT a bare 200 on generic port 8085 (Spring Boot etc). An open S3/Azure/GCS bucket with a backups/ prefix is only Velero if a velero-backup.json object sits inside backups/<name>/.

deployment_tells: /metrics on 8085 returns velero_backup_* gauges with {schedule=...} and {backupName=...} labels naming every backup
/debug/pprof/ on 6060 present only when --profiler-address is enabled (pprof metadata-leak sibling)
Third-party UIs (otwld velero-ui /api/v1/backups, seriohub VUI) expose HTTP/WebSocket backup-listing if deployed without their auth layer
pivot_paths: GET /metrics | grep '^velero_backup' — read velero_backup_total (count of existing backups) and harvest backup/schedule names from {schedule=...} and {backupName=...} labels. NAMES ONLY.

velero_backup_last_status (1/0) + velero_backup_last_successful_timestamp{schedule=...} reveal which schedules exist and their last success time — operator/freshness profiling without touching the store

Pivot to snapshot store ONLY if the BackupStorageLocation bucket is independently world-readable: list keys under backups/ (S3 ?prefix=backups/ or az/gsutil ls) to enumerate backup folder names — mirrors Velero's own folder-listing, metadata layer only

For each backup of interest read the small metadata objects backups/<name>/velero-backup.json and resource-list.json.gz to learn includedNamespaces and captured CRD kinds — apply AI-scope discriminator here
List (do not fetch) restic/ and kopia/<namespace>/ prefixes to confirm which namespaces have PV-level data captured; the namespace appears in the path itself
STOP at the manifest. contents.tar.gz, the kopia repo blobs, any *.tar.gz is the actual cluster snapshot — exfil, out of bounds
vulnerabilities: CVE-2020-3996: Velero restore package improperly manages volume identifiers, causing information leakage to unauthorized users; fixed 1.4.3 / 1.5.2
CVE-2025-58181: vulnerability affecting velero and velero-restore-helper (restore-time handling); fixed in 1.17.1-r2 image build
CVE-2024-45338: golang.org/x/net (vendored into velero-plugin-for-aws) non-linear parse complexity DoS; transitive image CVE
CVE-2024-34158: go/build/constraint stack-exhaustion in velero-plugin-for-csi image (transitive Go stdlib); image-level
